tellings.quote: so what did we learn in 1911 we learned that when a material breaks the laws of physics when anything does it's actually probably because it's an emergent property or an immersion phenomenon right of underlying strange quantum mechanics that are going on

plain: A young researcher, Deep Prasad, points to 1911, when a scientist named Onnes discovered superconductivity, materials that carry electricity with no resistance at all. Prasad says the lesson was that when something seems to break the laws of physics, it is probably an effect that grows out of strange quantum behaviour underneath. He uses this to suggest that UAP, the official term for unexplained flying objects, might behave impossibly for the same kind of reason.
